title: "Sockeye salmon TagSeq: territorial vs social"

date: today

This is the rendered analysis for the Berdahl sockeye salmon TagSeq experiment.
Every number and figure below comes from re-running the notebooks in this
repository; nothing is transcribed by hand.

Reproduce it with `renv::restore()` followed by `./render-all.sh` from the
project root. See the [repository
README](https://github.com/RobertsLab/project-sockeye-tagseq#reproducibility)
for the entry point and the expected-difference statement, and
`REPRODUCIBILITY-PLAN.md` for the audit trail behind the current state of the
code.

## Design

TagSeq (3'-end mRNA sequencing) of two tissues from fish assigned to two
behavioural treatments, territorial and social.

| Tissue | Samples sequenced | Territorial | Social | Analysed | Excluded |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Liver | 30 (`B01`–`B30`) | 15 | 15 | 30 | — |
| Gonad | 30 (`C01`–`C30`) | 15 | 15 | 28 | `C05`, `C17` |

Counts are gene-level, quantified against NCBI assembly
[GCF_006149115.2 (Oner_1.1)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_006149115.2/):
37,942 genes before filtering. Treatment contrast is territorial vs social with
`social` as the reference level, tested with DESeq2 and reported at
`padj < 0.05`.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The two excluded gonad samples are not yet reproducibly justified

`C05` and `C17` are dropped by a hardcoded `exclude` in `tag-seq/code/_common.R`,
on the basis of a MultiQC sample-correlation inspection whose output is **not in
this repository** — `tag-seq/QC/multiqc_gonad/` contains only a placeholder.
This is the one analytical choice with a discretionary effect on the gonad
results, and it currently rests on a statement rather than on evidence (audit
findings R5 and E9). Treat the gonad counts as provisional until either the
MultiQC output is committed or the exclusion criterion is computed inside
notebook 02.
:::

## Results as committed

Differential expression, territorial vs social, `padj < 0.05`, `apeglm`
shrinkage:

| Tissue | Genes tested | Significant | Characterized | Uncharacterized |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Liver | 5,646 | 31 | 31 | 0 |
| Gonad | 18,935 | 1,630 | 1,587 | 41 |

Rows with no annotation available: 11 of 5,646 (liver), 12 of 18,935 (gonad).
"Uncharacterized" means NCBI describes the gene as `uncharacterized LOC…`;
2.5% of the significant gonad genes.

Enrichment, FDR < 0.05:

| Tissue | GO terms tested | GO enriched | KEGG pathways tested | KEGG enriched |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Liver | 3,749 | 0 | 191 | 0 |
| Gonad | 6,066 | 35 | 195 | 6 |

Both use `goseq`'s hypergeometric over-representation test, GO against the NCBI
GO annotation for this assembly (155,362 annotations, 32,629 genes, 6,937 terms)
and KEGG against organism `one`, Benjamini–Hochberg corrected. The gonad signal
is ribosomal and mitochondrial: the top KEGG pathways are oxidative
phosphorylation (`one00190`, 59 of 188 genes, FDR 2e-16) and ribosome
(`one03010`, 66 of 262, FDR 2e-13), and the top GO terms are structural
constituent of ribosome, translation and the mitochondrial respiratory chain.

`goseq`'s default Wallenius test, which re-weights genes by transcript length,
is not used. TagSeq is 3′-end counting, so read count does not scale with
length; the length association in these data runs the other way, with short
genes far more likely to be differentially expressed; and the Wallenius result
turned out to depend on the platform, with the three terms it called at FDR
0.004–0.045 on macOS falling to 0.057–0.081 on Linux. The reasoning is set out
in notebook 04.

That the liver comparison yields no enriched terms is a result, not a failure:
31 significant genes is little power for an over-representation test.

## Result tables

Tracked in git, so a re-render either reproduces them or shows a diff:

- [`tag-seq/DESEQ_output/`](https://github.com/RobertsLab/project-sockeye-tagseq/tree/main/tag-seq/DESEQ_output) — per-tissue DESeq2 tables (unshrunken plus `normal`, `apeglm` and `ashr` shrinkage), PCA, heatmaps, volcano and MA plots
- [`tag-seq/gene_tables/`](https://github.com/RobertsLab/project-sockeye-tagseq/tree/main/tag-seq/gene_tables) — significant genes split by annotation status, and the LOC identifier lists
- [`tag-seq/GO_output/`](https://github.com/RobertsLab/project-sockeye-tagseq/tree/main/tag-seq/GO_output) — full and FDR-filtered GO and KEGG results

## Data availability

Raw FASTQ files are on Gannet:
<https://gannet.fish.washington.edu/seashell/bu-github/project-sockeye-tagseq/>.

They have **no archival accession yet** — no BioProject, no SRA (audit finding
E10). Until they are deposited, the raw data has neither a persistence guarantee
nor a citable identifier, and the analysis cannot be re-derived from source by
anyone outside the lab. The committed count matrices are checksummed in
`CHECKSUMS.sha256` and verified at the start of every render, which pins what
this analysis was run on but does not substitute for the deposit.
